title: Development of tracheobronchial fluid for in vitro bioaccessibility assessment of particulates-bound trace elements
author: Olumayede, Oguntimehin, et al.
materials: All chemicals used in this work were of analytical grade and were used without further purification. Glycine and cysteine were purchased from Sigma Aldrich, UK. Anhydrous sodium sulphates (Na2SO4), sodium chloride (NaCl), CaCl2, NaHPO4, NaHCO3, KCl, MgCl2, were purchased from Merck, London. Potassium Chloride (KCl), were obtained from BDH. Ascorbic acid, uric acid, glutathione, albumin, cysteine, glycine and polyethylene oxide resin were products of Sigma-Aldrich. All experimental solutions were prepared using double deionized water (MilliQ system, Millipores).

steps.title: Prepare inorganic phase
steps.instruction: Weigh accurately 6020 mg NaCl, 256 mg CaCl₂, 150 mg NaHPO₄, 2700 mg NaHCO₃, 298 mg KCl, 200 mg MgCl₂, and 72 mg Na₂SO₄; transfer them to a 500 mL high‑density polyethylene (HDPE) bottle, add ultra‑pure water (MilliQ) and make up the volume to 500 mL, then mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Prepare organic phase
steps.instruction: Weigh accurately 18 mg ascorbic acid, 16 mg uric acid, and 30 mg glutathione; place them in a separate 500 mL HDPE bottle, add ultra‑pure water and make up the volume to 500 mL, then mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Combine phases with macromolecules
steps.instruction: Pour both the inorganic and organic 500 mL solutions into a 2 L conical flask that already contains 260 mg albumin, 122 mg cysteine, 100 mg locus‑bean gum, 376 mg glycine, and 500 mg mucin; mix the contents thoroughly until all components are completely dissolved, yielding a total of 1000 mL of locus‑bean‑substituted synthetic lung fluid.

steps.title: Measure physical characteristics
steps.instruction: Determine the fluid’s pH with a PHS‑3C meter (UK), density with a pycnometer, conductivity with a Jenway A520 meter (UK) using 0.01 M KCl as reference, viscosity with a capillary viscometer, and surface tension using the drop‑weight method (modified as described in reference [9]).
